task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-225's implementation against its validated design and all 7 acceptance criteria, including all 11 rules' independent fixturability.

result.note: Design fidelity: lib/letflow/entities/definition.ex, .../definition/validator.ex, .../definition/shape.ex match the design's module names, @type shapes, and §7 function signatures (validate/1, Violation struct with rule/path/message, content_hash/1, logical_shape_of/1) exactly. No deviation found. Independently re-ran (mix via ~/.asdf/shims, not trusting ELIXIR-DEV's numbers): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` after touching all 3 lib files -- clean, zero output/warnings. `mix format --check-formatted` on the 5 new files -- exit 0, no diffs. `mix test test/letflow/entities/definition/validator_test.exs test/letflow/entities/definition/shape_test.exs` -- 'Finished in 0.1 seconds ... Result: 37 passed', 0 failures (confirmed via real ExUnit output, seed 382794). Per-rule fixture independence verified by reading every test: Rule 1 (name_format, uppercase/length fixtures, path [:name]), Rule 2 (duplicate_name, 3 separately-fixtured scopes: fields/indexes/fk+constraint-combined, each asserting the single expected violation), Rule 3 (queried_json_conflict, single json+queried field), Rule 4 (index_field_not_found and index_field_not_queried as two distinct sub-fixtures), Rule 5 (fk_field_not_found via both an FK and a constraint fixture, distinguished by path prefix), Rule 6 (invalid_enum, 3 sub-fixtures: absent/duplicate/present-on-non-enum), Rule 7 (invalid_decimal, 3 sub-fixtures: missing/scale>precision/present-on-non-decimal), Rule 8a/8b/8c (too_many_fields at 201, too_many_indexes at 33, too_many_fk_or_constraints at both a 33/0 split and a 20/13 mixed split proving the combined ceiling), Rule 9 (self_referential_fk). Each fixture uses the minimal valid skeleton (name/display_name/one field) plus exactly the one violating element, and each assertion pattern-matches the exact expected violation list (mostly single-element, confirming no other rule accidentally trips) -- this holds up under inspection, not just per ELIXIR-DEV's count claim. Canonicalisation reuse confirmed genuine: shape.ex's private hash_via_canonicaliser/1 calls `Jason.encode!/1` then `Letflow.Repository.Canonicaliser.canonicalize_content("application/json", json_bytes)` and `Letflow.Repository.Canonicaliser.content_hash/1` directly (grepped and read source) -- no second canonicalisation/hashing algorithm exists anywhere in the 3 new lib files (grep for Repo./Ecto.Schema/hash/sort in lib/letflow/entities/ found only the moduledoc's own delegation description). Logical-shape-versioning tests genuinely exercise the design: shape_test.exs proves field/list reordering, display_name change, and description change do NOT bump logical_shape_of/1's digest (while explicitly also asserting the raw content_hash DOES change for the reordering case, correctly distinguishing the two), and proves field addition, field-type change, and field removal DO bump it -- matching design §5's worked examples exactly, not a weaker substitute check. AC1 has two direct tests (a fully-populated internally-consistent document and a minimal one) both asserting validate/1 == :ok. Scope discipline confirmed via `git diff 97250f7e..3d608cfb --stat`: exactly the 5 files ELIXIR-DEV claimed (definition.ex, definition/shape.ex, definition/validator.ex, and their two test files), 1208 insertions, 0 deletions -- no migration, no persistence/CRUD context module, no ArtifactKind extension, no route/controller file, matching the design's explicit NOT-IN-SCOPE list and AC6. Idiom/OTP: this is pure functional validation logic as expected -- no GenServer/gen_statem/spawn/process machinery anywhere in the new files (grepped), consistent with lib/letflow/repository/canonicaliser.ex's own style (moduledoc-heavy, @typedoc-per-shape, plain pipelines and pattern-matched private helpers, no hidden state). No Repo call, migration, or route registration found anywhere in the new files -- confirmed this genuinely does not touch a tenant-data path, so no SECURITY-REVIEWER gate applies. No scope creep: nothing beyond the design's §7 public API was added (no extra convenience functions, no speculative abstractions); the malformed-shape precondition and its helper functions are exactly what design §3's preamble specifies, not an addition. Overall: idiomatic, correctly scoped, design-faithful. PASS -- clear to proceed to TEST-DESIGNER (ELIXIR-DEV's existing tests already provide the comprehensive coverage TEST-DESIGNER would otherwise need to author, consistent with this session's established pattern for well-specified low-risk requirements; TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should still confirm coverage independently rather than rubber-stamping this review).
